counterfactual_missing_items: Carcinoembryonic antigen was 1.69 ng/mL (within normal range)
decisive_items: invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception
Colonoscopy revealed a 5 × 5 cm exophytic mass at the descending–sigmoid junction occupying half of the lumen

Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen demonstrated a well-defined hypodense lesion measuring 4.6 × 3.4 cm with fat density in the sigmoid-colon wall protruding into the lumen, along with invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception
response.rationale: R6 is the most likely diagnosis due to the presence of invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon, which is consistent with intussusception. The colonoscopy and CT findings also support this diagnosis.

rejected.why: R8 is less likely due to the lack of specific findings supporting a polyp or mass as the primary diagnosis.
R2 is less likely due to the normal carcinoembryonic antigen level, which makes cancer less likely.
R7 is less likely due to the lack of specific findings supporting diverticulitis as the primary diagnosis.
R1 is less likely due to the lack of specific findings supporting inflammatory bowel disease as the primary diagnosis.
